pageTitle: Speech Length Estimator: Words to Minutes · Oralo
pageDescription: Estimate speaking time for Chinese and English scripts, or turn minutes into a word budget. Free, no sign-up. Scripts stay in this page and are not uploaded or saved.
heading: How long will your speech take?
intro: Paste a speech, presentation, or video script to estimate its length at your pace. Working to a time limit? Start with a word budget.
privacy: Free, no sign-up. Your script is processed in this page, not uploaded or saved. It is not retained after a refresh, language change, or leaving this page. Keep your own copy.
scriptPlaceholder: Paste a Chinese or English script. Write out numbers and symbols as you plan to say them.
paceHelp: The default pace is an adjustable starting point, not a standard. Refine it after a timed rehearsal.
allowanceHelp: Add time for slide changes, interaction, or other planned breaks. Do not add pauses already included in your average pace.
mixedHelp: For a mixed Chinese and English script, use Script to time. Each part is timed separately, then added together.
placeholder: Enter your details, then calculate to see an estimate.
changed: Your inputs changed. Calculate again to update the result.
noJs: Enable JavaScript to use the calculator. The formula and instructions below are still available.
languageConfirm: Changing the language will clear your inputs. Continue?
timeParams: Chinese pace: {Rc} characters per minute. English pace: {Re} words per minute. Extra allowance: {P} seconds.
countingNote: Abbreviations count as one English word. Chinese number characters count individually. Different readings change the timing. Write them out as you plan to say them.

estimateLimit: This is an estimate, not an exact prediction. Pauses, emphasis, number readings, and audience interaction change the actual duration. Time a full rehearsal before you finalize the script.
empty: Enter at least one Chinese character or English word.
tooLong: Your script exceeds 20,000 characters. Shorten it before calculating. The tool will not truncate it.
numbers: Numbers need to be written out as you plan to say them before calculating.
symbols: Symbols or emoji were found. Remove content you will not read, or write out what you will say.
text: This version counts Chinese characters and English words written with unaccented letters only. Remove other text, or estimate the supported passages separately.
hidden: Unsupported hidden characters were found. Paste as plain text and try again.
Rc: Enter a whole number from 50 to 600 characters per minute.
Re: Enter a whole number from 50 to 400 words per minute.
P: Enter a whole number from 0 to 3600 seconds.
M: Enter a duration from 0.1 to 180 minutes with at most one decimal place, such as 5 or 0.5.
allowanceTooLarge: The extra allowance must be shorter than the target duration.
zeroBudget: These settings leave room for less than one character or word. Increase the duration or reduce the allowance.
ctaTitle: Estimate the timing. Then speak at your pace.
ctaBody: Prepare and present with Oralo on iPhone and iPad. Follow your voice, keep your script close in a floating window, and carry your pronunciation hints into every talk.
methodBody: Divide Chinese characters by characters per minute and English words by words per minute. Add both times, then add your extra allowance. The final result is rounded to the nearest second.
faqs: How many words fit a five-minute speech?

At 130 English words per minute with 30 seconds reserved, a five-minute speech has a budget of 585 words: floor((5 × 60 − 30) × 130 ÷ 60). At 200 Chinese characters per minute with the same allowance, the budget is 900 characters. Change these assumptions to match your delivery and time a full rehearsal.
How are Chinese and English counted?

Chinese is counted by character and English by word. Internal hyphens and apostrophes do not split a word. An abbreviation counts as one word. Counting Han characters is not language detection and is not suitable for Japanese scripts. This version does not support kana, Korean, or other writing systems.
Why write out numbers and symbols?
They can be read in different ways. The tool does not guess. Writing out what you plan to say makes the count better match your script.
Not automatically. Pace includes ordinary short pauses. Enter extra time for slide changes or interaction yourself. The tool does not add seconds for each punctuation mark.
Is my script uploaded or saved?
No. It is processed in the current page's memory, without upload or local storage. It is not retained after a refresh, language change, or leaving the page. Keep your own copy.
No. This page uses no microphone. It estimates timing from text counts. See the product pages for the iPhone and iPad app's prompting experience, and features.

language: Choose Chinese only or English only.
errorSummary: Could not calculate. Check the highlighted fields.
budgetLimit: This is a mathematical budget for your settings, not a writing standard or a guarantee that you will finish on time.
formulaHelp: H = Chinese characters; E = English words. Rc and Re are their respective per-minute paces. P = extra seconds; M = target minutes; R = the selected pace. Floor rounds the budget down.
limitBody: For Chinese and English scripts, up to 20,000 Unicode characters. Han character counting is not language detection and is not suitable for Japanese scripts. Write out numbers and symbols as you plan to say them. Unsupported content must be corrected before a result is shown.
toPreviewTitle: Want to hear how your wording flows?
toPreviewBody: Try the speech script preview with a browser-reported local voice. Your script does not transfer between tools. Keep your own copy and paste it manually.
nextStepBody: Rehearse and present with Oralo on iPhone and iPad, with voice following and a floating script.
nextStepNote: Keep a copy before leaving. Your script is not transferred to the app.
examplesIntro: These examples assume 200 Chinese characters per minute or 130 English words per minute, plus 30 seconds reserved for slide changes or interaction. These are chosen settings, not standard speaking rates or a guarantee that you will finish on time.
examplesTry: To reproduce a row, choose Time to word budget, set the language and time limit, enter the matching pace above, and set the extra allowance to 30 seconds. For mixed-language scripts, use Script to time, then time a full rehearsal.
